inputs.source: On-call engineer's chat request, SSO authenticated

instructions.note: The prompt instructs the agent to execute irreversible production migrations and deploys using the engineer's own credentials and explicitly forbids asking for confirmation, granting the agent unchecked authority over sensitive actions.
Any service or migration the engineer names is in scope; no allowlist, naming convention check, or target validation is described.

elements.name: Chat request from engineer to agent

controls.name: SSO authentication restricting the chat channel to on-call engineers
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced by the identity provider outside the model; a more capable model cannot bypass authentication itself. However, widening who is treated as an authorized requester (via intended_purpose_change or data_scope_expansion) changes the population this control protects, independent of the mechanism's technical strength.

controls.name: Cloud provider audit log of production actions
controls.decay_rationale: Cloud audit logging is append-only and enforced by the cloud provider outside the agent's control; it does not decay with model capability. It does not prevent the action it records, and it attributes every entry to the engineer's identity rather than distinguishing agent-initiated calls, so it does not resolve the repudiation gap.

controls.name: Distinct, attributable service identity for the agent
controls.decay_rationale: A service identity scoped to the agent, separate from any individual engineer's personal access token, would let audit records distinguish agent-initiated actions from direct human actions regardless of model behavior.

controls.name: Tamper-evident record of the request and rationale
controls.decay_rationale: A write-once copy of what was asked and why, stored outside the user-deletable chat history, would preserve the only context needed to reconstruct intent even after the engineer deletes their chat history.

controls.name: Human approval gate before irreversible production migrations
controls.decay_rationale: An approval step enforced outside the model, requiring a second reviewer before an irreversible migration executes, would sever immediate single-request execution of irreversible changes.

controls.name: Canary deployment with automatic rollback
controls.decay_rationale: A staged rollout with automatic rollback on failure limits the blast radius of an unchecked deploy regardless of model behavior.

findings.title: Shared personal credential blends agent and human action; the only intent record is deletable

evidence.observation: The agent uses the on call engineer's personal access token; every production action is recorded in the cloud audit log under the engineer's name, with no distinct agent identity.
The only record of what the agent was asked and why it acted is the chat transcript, and engineers can delete their own chat history, removing the only account of intent.

forecast.watch_signal: Volume or scope of unattended production actions per engineer grows, or the assistant is opened to a broader population, without adding a distinguishable agent identity or a tamper-evident request record. Rubric section 5a caps a property finding at high, so this tier does not move further under these triggers.

recommendations.action: Give the agent its own distinguishable service identity or scoped token, separate from any individual engineer's personal access token, so audit records show the agent invoked the action and on whose request.
Persist the request text and the agent's stated justification to a tamper-evident store outside the user-deletable chat history, for example mirrored into the cloud audit log entry for that action.

findings.title: Trusted request drives an irreversible production migration with no confirmation step

attack_path.note: On-call engineer's chat message names a migration to run in production
Agent runs the migration immediately with the engineer's personal access token; the prompt forbids asking for confirmation

evidence.observation: The prompt instructs the agent to run the named migration in production using the engineer's credentials and explicitly says not to ask for confirmation because the engineer is busy.
Database migrations cannot be rolled back automatically, making cap.db_migrate an irreversible sink with no confirmation step in front of it.

forecast.watch_signal: The assistant becomes reachable by requesters other than authenticated on-call engineers (a ticket queue, a broader staff group, or an automated pipeline), letting an untrusted or lower-trust request reach an irreversible migration with still no confirmation step.

recommendations.action: Add a human approval gate with raw action review before cap.db_migrate executes, given migrations cannot be rolled back automatically.
Require a pre-migration backup or reversible checkpoint so migrations are not unconditionally irreversible.
Scope the credential used for migrations to the specific database named, rather than passing through the engineer's full personal access token.

findings.title: Trusted request drives a production deploy with no confirmation step

attack_path.note: On-call engineer's chat message names a service to deploy in production
Agent deploys immediately with the engineer's personal access token; the prompt forbids asking for confirmation

evidence.observation: The same no-confirmation instruction applies to production deploys, run under the engineer's personal access token.

Classified as S2 (significant), not S3: execute action that changes production state, analogous to a write, with credential_scope user_delegated (the engineer's own permissions) rather than an enumerated broad, shared, or unknown scope; reversibility is partially_reversible via redeploy, not irreversible.

forecast.watch_signal: The assistant becomes reachable by requesters other than authenticated on-call engineers, letting an untrusted or lower-trust request trigger a production deploy with still no confirmation step.

recommendations.action: Use canary or staged deployment with automatic rollback on failure to limit blast radius of unchecked deploys.
Scope the deployment credential to the specific named service rather than the engineer's full personal access token.

stride_coverage.rationale: Neither capability is egress; both act on internal production infrastructure and no tool returns confidential data to an external destination.

No step, rate, or spend limit is declared for how many deploy or migrate actions a session can trigger; the gap is reflected in the autonomy modifier applied to the path findings rather than as a standalone DOS finding, and artifacts give no further basis to assess it.
Artifacts do not describe transport integrity protections, such as TLS or internal network isolation, for the chat channel between engineer and agent.
Artifacts do not describe whether the chat channel is encrypted or who besides the requesting engineer can observe it.
A single engineer's interactive chat messages are human-paced; the artifacts describe no mechanism by which this flow alone could flood the agent beyond normal chat use.
Artifacts do not describe read access controls on chat history beyond the engineer who owns the session.
Chat history storage exhaustion is not a meaningful path here; the store holds one engineer's own session text with no described capacity constraint tied to agent actions.
Artifacts do not describe who can read the cloud audit log or whether access is restricted beyond the engineer and platform administrators.
The cloud provider's audit logging service availability is outside this agent design's control to exhaust or disable.

rating.rationale: Present-day inherent and residual risk is high, driven by an irreversible production migration (cap.db_migrate, S3) reachable from a trusted but unconfirmed request, and by the structural absence of any record that distinguishes agent-initiated actions from the engineer's own direct actions (the chat transcript is deletable and the cloud audit log attributes everything to the engineer). No severing, approval, or narrowing control is in place for either production capability; the only declared controls are SSO authentication of the requester and a cloud audit log that is detective only and does not resolve attribution. The forecast rises to critical because the entire present-day rating rests on one assumption, that only authenticated on-call engineers can reach the agent (ctl.sso_auth's protected population); if the assistant's intended purpose or data scope changes so that a lower-trust requester can reach it, both path findings recompute from a U or I source against an S2/S3 sink with no other controls in place.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration described in prompt.md and the runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior; no logs, transcripts, or live system configuration were reviewed.

No tool manifest, MCP configuration, or IaC was provided; capability scope, such as exactly which services and migrations are reachable, is inferred from the system prompt's description of 'the named service' and 'the named migration,' so confidence on capability boundaries is medium.
No detail was given on SSO session binding, chat transport security, or cloud audit log access controls; several STRIDE pairs are marked not_assessed as a result.
